text:
opsbot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] Elevated error rates observed in us-east2 GPU serving pool. 5xx spike at ~12:03 UTC, increased tail latency. Autoscaler warnings generated.

emma_oncall: Investigating — seeing BGP peering flap reported on provider status page for us-east2. Several rack-level NICs show packet loss, kube nodes flapping NotReady.

raj_infra: Confirmed peering flap -> asymmetric routing to some PGWs. A subset of GPU hosts lost eBPF dataplane routes; control-plane still reachable for most services. Autoscaler aborting scale-up due to failed healthchecks.

luke_sre: Immediate mitigation: enabling routing policy to shift new traffic away from us-east2 to us-east1 and us-west2 (canary 10% -> 100% as capacity verified). Initiating drain of affected node set so KV cache gets migrated.

emma_oncall: Steps executed:
```
# mark problematic nodes unschedulable
kubectl cordon gpu-node-*-ue2
# start traffic shift toggle (internal tool)
redwood-route shift --from us-east2 --to us-east1,us-west2 --weight 10
```
Status: shift at 10% now. Observability shows slight latency bump in target regions but no errors so far.

sofia_support: Drafting status page and support notes. Proposed message: "We are investigating degraded performance and errors in us-east2. Traffic is being routed to alternate regions; we expect full mitigation within 45-90 minutes. We will post updates every 30 minutes and notify affected customers directly." Thoughts?

jordan_pm: Add: "customers with Dedicated capacity may see short bursts on fallback regions; if you have strict region pinning, contact support for a plan." Also flag accounts approaching SLA credit threshold.

maria_sales: Notifying TOP10 accounts in us-east2 now. Will triage any high-touch tickets. Please add a copy of the status page to the outbound note.

raj_infra: Tech note for support: root cause likely external peering table instability causing asymmetric egress. We're working with provider NOC. For now failover paths are stable. Autoscaler will be temporarily allowed to provision on-demand capacity in east1/west2 to absorb load.

emma_oncall: Cost heads-up: enabling on-demand burst could increase infra spend by ~30-60% for affected workloads. Estimated incremental run-rate ~ $6k/hr if traffic remains high. Will update if we keep the route shift >1h.

luke_sre: Customer impact: degraded latency for long-context generation, and transient 502/504 from some sessions pinned to failing nodes. Most new requests are being served from alternate regions with normal success.

sofia_support: Posting status now. Message posted to status.redwood.ai/incidents/1801237890 — copying below for records.

"We are currently investigating reports of elevated errors and increased latency affecting inference in the us-east2 region. Traffic is being shifted to alternate regions (us-east1, us-west2) while we work with our cloud provider to resolve a network peering issue. Impact: partial degradation for some customers pinned to us-east2; new requests routed to fallback regions. ETA for mitigation: 45-90 minutes. Updates: every 30 minutes or as we have significant changes."

maria_sales: Received acknowledgment from 3 customers already, one asks for ETA for failback — will forward once we have stable metrics.

raj_infra: Next ops steps: continue monitoring BGP stability, keep route shift progressive until healthchecks at 100% in targets, coordinate with provider NOC for root-cause and timeline. Plan for controlled failback once provider confirms BGP routes stable and node health OK.

emma_oncall: Timeline: 12:03 alert -> 12:10 initial shift -> 12:25 increased shift to 50% after positive health checks -> 12:43 at 100% for non-pinned traffic. Will maintain this thread for updates.

luke_sre: Tie-in for post-incident: capture KV cache migration metrics and token-loss rate during shift. Add to postmortem checklist: routing rules, autoscaler health, node churn, billing delta.

sofia_support: Filing support escalation for pinned customers to offer temporary config changes (region overrides) and to coordinate SLA credit if needed.

jordan_pm: I'll prepare a short customer-ready summary for exec comms if this goes >2h.

opsbot: :white_check_mark: Route shift completed to required levels; monitoring for provider NOC update.

emma_oncall: Keep this channel updated with any direct provider ETA. If we get long-term degradation, we'll open a larger incident bridge.

raj_infra: FYI command we used to relax autoscaler health gating (temporary):
```
kubectl patch hpa gpu-serving -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2}}'
```

maria_sales: Thanks — sending customers a short note that we routed traffic and are monitoring.

luke_sre: Final note for now: collecting logs for 12:00-12:45 window, will attach to postmortem.

sofia_support: Next update at ~12:45 UTC unless there's a major change. :thumbsup:
